description.de: Erzeugt die Erdmaennchen-Illustrationen des Willkommens-Rundgangs ueber die Codex-CLI — alle in EINEM Lauf, damit sie ein Satz werden. Die Prompts sind kuratiert (Stil-Steckbrief plus eine Szene je Panel in walkthroughImagePrompts.json); kein KI-Schritt formuliert sie um, denn genau das erzeugt Stildrift. Geprueft wird dreistufig: mechanisch (Masse, Groesse, Randfarbe, Farbklima), durch Codex' eigenen Blick (Text, Logos, Anzahl Erdmaennchen — es gibt kein OCR auf dem Host) und zuletzt durch einen Menschen, denn ob ein Bild das Richtige sagt, kann keine Messung entscheiden. Erst nach der Freigabe wird das Manifest geschrieben; bis dahin zeigt die Anwendung nichts. Nur auf dem Dev-Host lauffaehig.
description.en: Generates the meerkat illustrations of the welcome walkthrough via the Codex CLI — all in ONE run so they form a set. The prompts are curated (style sheet plus one scene per panel in walkthroughImagePrompts.json); no AI step rewords them, because that is exactly what causes style drift. Checking has three stages: mechanical (dimensions, size, border colour, colour climate), Codex's own look (text, logos, number of meerkats — there is no OCR on the host) and finally a person, because no measurement can decide whether a picture says the right thing. The manifest is written only after approval; until then the application shows nothing. Runs on the dev host only.

author: MySuricates
instructions: Image generation on the dev host. The blocks are pure shell blocks and access neither the REST API nor the database. Codex is called only to generate and to look at images, never to write or copy files.

config.command:
set -euo pipefail
command -v codex >/dev/null || { echo "ERROR: codex not in PATH. This workflow runs only on the dev host (Codex does not start in containers)."; exit 1; }
python3 -c "import PIL" 2>/dev/null || { echo "ERROR: Pillow is missing. The workflow uses it to normalize and measure the images."; exit 1; }
[ -f "ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImagePrompts.json" ] || { echo "ERROR: image concepts missing: ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImagePrompts.json"; exit 1; }
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
d = json.load(open("ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImagePrompts.json"))
assert d.get("stil"), "stil missing"
szenen = d.get("szenen") or {}
assert szenen, "no scenes"
print(f"Style sheet: {len(d['stil'])} characters")
print(f"Scenes: {len(szenen)} -> {', '.join(szenen)}")
print(f"Background: {d.get('hintergrund')} · Format: {d.get('format')}")
PY
mkdir -p "ai-automation-frontend/public/walkthrough"
echo "Output: $PWD/ai-automation-frontend/public/walkthrough"

config.items_command: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImagePrompts.json')); a=d.get('anker'); ids=list(d['szenen']); print(chr(10).join(([a] if a in ids else []) + [i for i in ids if i != a]))"
config.command:
set -euo pipefail
PANEL={{ panel }}
KONZEPT="ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImagePrompts.json"
OUT="ai-automation-frontend/public/walkthrough/$PANEL.png"
GENDIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/generated_images"
MARKER="$(mktemp)"

ANKER=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$KONZEPT')).get('anker') or '')")
ANKERBILD="ai-automation-frontend/public/walkthrough/$ANKER.webp"

# The anchor fixes medium and figure and is created without a reference. Every further image gets
# it as a reference via -i: according to OpenAI's image guide an anchor image is the reliable way
# to keep style and character across a series — a text description alone is not enough,
# otherwise the model derives the medium from the materials of the scene (wood -> drawn,
# metal -> rendered). The requirements are repeated verbatim in every iteration.
# The anchor is the style decision, not a chance product: if it exists, it stays.
# Re-rolling it means deleting it — on purpose, not as a side effect of every run.
# Since the anchor holds the set together, consistency no longer depends on a shared run.
# Hence whatever already exists stays — single images are redone by deleting them.
if [ -f "${OUT%.png}.webp" ]; then
  echo "$PANEL: exists, stays unchanged (delete the file to regenerate it)"
  exit 0
fi

if [ "$PANEL" = "$ANKER" ] || [ ! -f "$ANKERBILD" ]; then
  TEXT=$(python3 -c "
import json
d = json.load(open('$KONZEPT'))
print(' '.join(x.strip() for x in (d['medium'], d['welt'], d['stil'], d['szenen']['$PANEL'])))
")
  REF=""
else
  TEXT=$(python3 -c "
import json
d = json.load(open('$KONZEPT'))
print('Match the attached reference image exactly in medium and character: same hand-painted look, '
      'same brush texture and shading, the same meerkat with the same face, proportions, clothing '
      'and colour palette, the same flat dark background and the same left-third placement. Do not '
      'redesign the character. Do not switch to a 3D or photorealistic render. Only the scene '
      'changes. New scene: ' + d['szenen']['$PANEL'].strip())
")
  # codex -i reliably takes PNG; the anchor image is stored as WebP.
  REF="$(mktemp --suffix=.png)"
  python3 -c "from PIL import Image; Image.open('$ANKERBILD').convert('RGB').save('$REF','PNG')"
fi

# Two documented traps (workflow ac4d041e):
# 1) stdin supplies the prompt and with it the EOF — without EOF codex exec hangs until the
#    block timeout. A trailing prompt argument does not work: -i is variadic and reads
#    it as a second image file ("No prompt provided via stdin").
# 2) Codex may ONLY generate — its bwrap sandbox does not start in the backend context. Hence
#    do not go through the imagegen skill either: for that, Codex would first read its SKILL.md via a
#    shell command. The copying is done below by the workflow's bash.
PROMPT="Use the built-in image_gen tool directly to create EXACTLY ONE square image. Do not read any files, do not open any skill documentation, do not run any shell command, do not validate and do not copy anything. Stop immediately after the image has been generated. Image description: $TEXT"
if [ -n "$REF" ]; then
  printf '%s' "$PROMPT" | timeout 300 codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox workspace-write -C "$PWD" -i "$REF" - >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  printf '%s' "$PROMPT" | timeout 300 codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox workspace-write -C "$PWD" - >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi

trap '[ -n "${REF:-}" ] && [ "${REF#/tmp/}" != "$REF" ] && rm -f "$REF"' EXIT
IMG=$(find "$GENDIR" -type f -name '*.png' -newer "$MARKER" -printf '%T@ %p\n' 2>/dev/null | sort -rn | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f2-)
rm -f "$MARKER"
[ -n "$IMG" ] && [ -f "$IMG" ] || { echo "ERROR $PANEL: no newly generated image in $GENDIR"; exit 1; }
cp "$IMG" "$OUT"
ROH=$(stat -c%s "$OUT")
python3 - "$OUT" <<'PY'
import sys
from PIL import Image
p = sys.argv[1]
im = Image.open(p)
# If the image comes back cut out (alpha), composite it onto the background colour on purpose —
# convert("RGB") alone puts it on black and leaves coloured fringes.
if im.mode in ("RGBA", "LA", "P"):
    im = im.convert("RGBA")
    grund = Image.new("RGBA", im.size, (0x1b, 0x17, 0x14, 255))
    im = Image.alpha_composite(grund, im)
im = im.convert("RGB")
w, h = im.size
s = min(w, h)
l, t = (w - s) // 2, (h - s) // 2
im = im.crop((l, t, l + s, t + s))
# Keep the native resolution (only cap it from above). Measured: WebP q88 at 1254 px is 132 KB,
# a 640 px PNG of the same source 525 KB — so the higher resolution costs nothing, and
# the same images are meant to feed the public site later.
if s > 1280:
    im = im.resize((1280, 1280), Image.LANCZOS)
im.save(p.rsplit(".", 1)[0] + ".webp", "WEBP", quality=88, method=6)
PY
rm -f "$OUT"
OUT="${OUT%.png}.webp"
echo "$PANEL${REF:+ (anchor: $ANKER)} -> $OUT (raw $((ROH/1024)) KB -> $(python3 -c "from PIL import Image; print('x'.join(map(str,Image.open('$OUT').size)))") WebP, $(($(stat -c%s "$OUT")/1024)) KB)"

set -euo pipefail
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os, sys
from collections import Counter
from PIL import Image

konzept = json.load(open("ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImagePrompts.json"))
ids = list(konzept["szenen"])
roh = konzept.get("hintergrund", "#1b1714").lstrip("#")
want_bg = tuple(int(roh[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))
outdir = "ai-automation-frontend/public/walkthrough"
# Border: colour distance up to which a border pixel counts as the background colour, and the minimum
# share of the background colour on the border. The approved set lies at 54-91 %.
RAND_TOLERANZ = 24
RAND_ANTEIL_MIN = 0.5

hart, weich, ok_ids = [], [], []
verteilungen = {}

for pid in ids:
    path = os.path.join(outdir, pid + ".webp")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        hart.append(f"{pid}: no file"); continue
    size = os.path.getsize(path)
    if size < 20_000:
        hart.append(f"{pid}: only {size} bytes — probably a failure"); continue
    if size > 400_000:
        weich.append(f"{pid}: {size//1024} KB, large for a panel")
    im = Image.open(path).convert("RGB")
    w, h = im.size
    if w != h:
        hart.append(f"{pid}: {w}x{h} not square — normalization failed"); continue
    if w < 900:
        hart.append(f"{pid}: only {w} px edge"); continue

    # Border = the outermost row of pixels all around. Its most frequent colour is measured, not an average
    # of a few points: a workbench that reaches the border covers only part of it and
    # does not shift the most frequent colour. The eight points used before measured metal there (notice, blocks).
    px = im.load()
    rand = ([px[x, 0] for x in range(w)] + [px[x, h-1] for x in range(w)]
            + [px[0, y] for y in range(1, h-1)] + [px[w-1, y] for y in range(1, h-1)])
    fach = Counter((r >> 4, g >> 4, b >> 4) for r, g, b in rand).most_common(1)[0][0]
    im_fach = [c for c in rand if (c[0] >> 4, c[1] >> 4, c[2] >> 4) == fach]
    grund = tuple(sum(c[i] for c in im_fach) // len(im_fach) for i in range(3))
    anteil = sum(1 for c in rand if max(abs(c[i] - grund[i]) for i in range(3)) <= RAND_TOLERANZ) / len(rand)
    abstand = max(abs(grund[i] - want_bg[i]) for i in range(3))
    grund_hex = "#%02x%02x%02x" % grund
    if abstand > RAND_TOLERANZ:
        weich.append(f"{pid}: border mostly {grund_hex} instead of #{want_bg[0]:02x}{want_bg[1]:02x}{want_bg[2]:02x} (distance {abstand})")
    if anteil < RAND_ANTEIL_MIN:
        weich.append(f"{pid}: only {anteil*100:.0f} % of the border in the background colour {grund_hex} — background uneven or the motif fills the border")
    klein = im.resize((64, 64))
    verteilungen[pid] = [sum(v) for v in zip(*[klein.getpixel((x, y)) for x in range(64) for y in range(64)])]

    ok_ids.append(pid)
    print(f"OK   {pid}: {w}x{h}, {size//1024} KB")

# Outliers in the colour climate: whatever falls out of the set is almost always style drift. Hue and
# brightness separately: the style fixes the hue (shares of R, G, B in the sum), whereas the brightness
# depends on the framing. A close-up with a large meerkat is brighter than a wide shot with
# a lot of dark background. Approved set: hue at most 2.0 percentage points from the mean,
# brightness -18 % (unattended) to +16 % (mix). The former channel threshold of 22 % measured both
# together and flagged mix only because of the framing.
FARBTON_MAX_PP = 3.5
HELLIGKEIT_MAX = 0.30
if len(verteilungen) >= 3:
    mittelwert = [sum(v[i] for v in verteilungen.values()) / len(verteilungen) for i in range(3)]
    mittel_summe = max(sum(mittelwert), 1)
    mittel_anteil = [m / mittel_summe for m in mittelwert]
    for pid, v in verteilungen.items():
        summe = max(sum(v), 1)
        farbton = max(abs(v[i] / summe - mittel_anteil[i]) for i in range(3)) * 100
        helligkeit = (summe - mittel_summe) / mittel_summe
        if farbton > FARBTON_MAX_PP:
            weich.append(f"{pid}: hue deviates {farbton:.1f} percentage points from the set")
        if abs(helligkeit) > HELLIGKEIT_MAX:
            weich.append(f"{pid}: brightness deviates {helligkeit*100:+.0f} % from the set")

print()
for zeile in weich: print("WARNING", zeile)
for zeile in hart: print("ERROR  ", zeile)
print()
print(f"{len(ok_ids)}/{len(ids)} images pass the hard check")
if hart:
    sys.exit(1)
PY

config.items_command: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImagePrompts.json')); a=d.get('anker'); ids=list(d['szenen']); print(chr(10).join(([a] if a in ids else []) + [i for i in ids if i != a]))"
config.command:
set -euo pipefail
PANEL={{ panel }}
BILD="ai-automation-frontend/public/walkthrough/$PANEL.webp"
[ -f "$BILD" ] || { echo "$PANEL: no image"; exit 1; }
# codex -i reliably takes PNG; the panel images are stored as WebP.
IMG="$(mktemp --suffix=.png)"; trap 'rm -f "$IMG"' EXIT
python3 -c "from PIL import Image; Image.open('$BILD').convert('RGB').save('$IMG','PNG')"
# No OCR on the host — the only available text check is Codex' own look.
# Background: a cross-check on 2026-10-04 with "a single flat dark colour" reported "subtle texture and
# shading" for 12 of 13 approved images. Whether the background is uniformly dark is measured by the block
# messen on the border; here it only matters whether a scene or a light background stands in place of the empty area.
# "-i" is variadic: a trailing prompt argument would be read as a second image file
# ("No prompt provided via stdin"). Hence the prompt goes via stdin with "-"; the pipe supplies the EOF.
FRAGE="Look at the attached image and answer in ONE line, nothing else. Run no commands. Answer exactly OK if ALL of these hold: no letters, no digits, no logos, no watermark anywhere; exactly one meerkat visible; the meerkat wears a dark technical harness and a head-mounted visor; the empty area behind the character and the objects is plain and dark; painted texture, soft shading and the glow of objects there are fine, a room, walls, windows, a landscape, sky or a light background are not; objects such as a workbench, tools or a conveyor belt are allowed. Otherwise answer PROBLEM: followed by what is wrong, in at most fifteen words."
ROH=$(printf '%s' "$FRAGE" | timeout 150 codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only -i "$IMG" - 2>/dev/null || true)
ANS=$(printf '%s' "$ROH" | grep -Eo '(PROBLEM:.*|OK)' | tail -1 || true)
echo "$PANEL: ${ANS:-NO ANSWER}"

set -euo pipefail
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os
konzept = json.load(open("ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImagePrompts.json"))
manifest = {}
for pid in konzept["szenen"]:
    if os.path.exists(os.path.join("ai-automation-frontend/public/walkthrough", pid + ".webp")):
        manifest[pid] = "/walkthrough/" + pid + ".webp"
with open("ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImages.json", "w") as fh:
    json.dump(manifest, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    fh.write("\n")
print(f"{len(manifest)} images entered in ai-automation-frontend/src/data/walkthroughImages.json")
for k, v in manifest.items():
    print(" ", k, "->", v)
PY
echo
echo "The application shows the images from now on. To undo: set the manifest to {}."
